summary: SYNTHETIC. Invented readers read PrompTugal.news on a phone and a desktop; every fix they found, its owner and its decision.

latest_line: run 5 (6 November, 04:40 UTC): four new readers, the homepage and one story each. All four could say how a story is made; none could say what 'signed' means or check it.
latest_intro: Four invented readers, a mix of expertise, all interested in technology, one who does not know what a prompt is. Each read the front page, picked the one story they would tap, read it to the end, and was asked how it was made, how they could check it and what 'signed' means. Live site v0.1.90 and v0.1.91; 231 screenshots, in the synthetic vault.

latest_readers.line: Stayed for 'a Porto cleantech spin-off'; would share it with her friend, not quote its figures without opening a source.
Read 'Who made this' like a CI pipeline; would share it with his AI club 'as an example of how to show provenance'.

latest_readers.line: Stayed for 'Every fact sourced'; would quote a fact after checking the Commission page, not share the article.

latest_signed: **'Signed' meant nothing they could use (F28).** Ana: 'the program put its stamp on it ... but I did not see any stamp'. Miguel: 'the page does not show the signature, the key or how to verify'. Helena: 'Honestly, I do not know'. Tom: 'a claim I have to take on trust'. Measured: the signature is served (articles/<slug>.md.sig) and the key is public (board/keys.json); no article links either.
latest_held: 'What this does not claim'; every source with the date published and the date read; 'In short'; About's rules. In plain words, the provenance works: all four told how a story was made, correctly, in their own words.
latest_lost: the £ balance dropping when a story opens (F01, all four); bylines read as email handles, no accountable human named (F14, all four); insider words in 'Who made this' (F30); the code box and plain-text link unexplained (F29); a second homepage screen that says 'for attendees' (F32). Measured: 7 of 11 articles scroll sideways on a phone (F10).

Outreach's revised Portuguese email moved her from 'maybe, leaning no' to 'maybe, leaning yes, but not today'.

With the flows mapped and the disclosure quoted in the email, she forwarded the page to her product owner; still no call (F25).

method: **Who:** synthetic@PrompTugal.dinis, one Claude sub-agent per invented reader, after synthetic@web-summit.indi's method on the team site (WS-142). Each reader sees screenshots only (390 x 844 phone, 1280 x 800 desktop, Playwright and Chromium on the live site), never the code; page-view counting is paused for every capture, so no synthetic read is counted as a reader. Each claim a reader makes about the site is checked against the page text or its source before it becomes a fix (run 4: a flagged 'error' was faithful to the source and was dropped).

**Where the material is:** every screenshot, page text and run in a public vault (qourr7be on dev.send.sgraph.ai; read key in [vault.json](https://github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website/blob/dev/desks/synthetic/vault.json)), not in the repository, at Dinis's word. The repository keeps the runs, the notes to each agent and the ledger.

**When a run happens:** only when the pages changed. [changes.mjs](https://github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website/blob/dev/desks/synthetic/tools/changes.mjs) compares each page's markdown twin with what the readers last saw (5-word shingles, versions and the meter left out): a run when a page changed 20%, the front page's first screen 10%, or a new article is on the front page. Within the pass's budget (accountant@, board/budgets.json), never looping on its own findings.
